question: Q7 - Years in noncompliance, zero consequences: EPA ECHO facilities by quarters in noncompliance (3-year window) split by whether any formal enforcement exists, plus a state ranking of chronic-and-unenforced facilities
finding: 15,323 facilities were in noncompliance every single quarter of the last three years and received zero formal enforcement actions; among all 54,315 chronic (8+ quarter) noncompliers, 82% (44,319) have no formal enforcement on file.
chart: Panel 1 (result.csv): stacked/grouped bar - x=QNC_BUCKET (ordered 0,1-3,4-7,8-11,12), y=FACILITIES, color=ENFORCEMENT; log y-scale or drop the '0' bucket since it dwarfs the rest (2.89M). Panel 2 (result_states.csv): horizontal bar of CHRONIC_ZERO_ENFORCEMENT by state, with PCT_CHRONIC_UNENFORCED as text/color.
caveats: QUARTERS_WITH_NONCOMPLIANCE caps at 12 - it is a 3-year rolling window, not lifetime; '12' means the entire observable window, and it is total quarters, not necessarily consecutive.
FORMAL_ACTION_COUNT / INFORMAL_ACTION_COUNT are ECHO's 5-year action counters; enforcement older than that window would not show.
~79k facilities (2.5%) have NULL quarters and are excluded.
State ranking filtered to states with >=50 chronic facilities.
notable: Monetary penalties appear ONLY where formal enforcement exists - all 5.9M facilities with zero formal actions also show zero penalties, confirming informal actions carry no fines.
Chronic-unenforced facilities still average 3-8 informal actions (letters, notices) - the paper trail exists, the consequences do not.
Washington state tops the count (2,972) and West Virginia the rate (91.6% of chronic noncompliers never formally enforced).
Even in the worst bucket (12/12 quarters), only 18% of facilities ever saw formal enforcement.
